intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim. Snorkeling gear can be rented locally to explore the rich marine life.
experiences.location: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Algarve Beachfront Wine Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a curated wine tasting session at a seaside wine bar in Lagos, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and local Syrah blends. A knowledgeable sommelier guides you through 5–6 wines paired with local cheeses, cured meats, and fresh bread, all enjoyed with views of the Atlantic Ocean.
experiences.location: Lagos Marina Waterfront, Lagos, Western Algarve

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil to the world-famous Benagil Cave, a breathtaking sea cathedral with a natural skylight opening. Your guide will lead you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the coastline. This small-group tour departs directly from the beach and includes all equipment and safety briefing.
experiences.location: Praia de Benagil, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise with Wine
experiences.description: Set sail along the stunning Algarve coastline aboard a catamaran as the sun dips below the horizon. The cruise includes a selection of local Algarve wines, sparkling water, and light snacks. Glide past iconic rock formations, sea arches, and golden cliffs while enjoying the warm Atlantic breeze — a perfect blend of your beach and wine interests.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day with Watersports
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most beautiful beaches in the Algarve stretching over 4 km. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, then try stand-up paddleboarding or windsurfing with a local instructor. The calm, shallow waters make it ideal for all skill levels. Beachside restaurants and bars are steps away for a relaxed lunch.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport around 13:00. Take the budget-friendly bus/shuttle or shared transfer to Lagoa (~1 hour). Check in to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Drop luggage and take a short 10-minute walk down to Praia da Marinha to catch the late afternoon golden light — one of the most stunning cove beaches in the Algarve. Explore the clifftop coastal path for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into Lagoa town centre (5 km, reachable by local bus or taxi). Grab a budget dinner at a local tasca (traditional Portuguese tavern). Try 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which typically costs €7–10 and includes bread, soup, main, and drink.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and espresso at the airport café on arrival (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Light snack from airport or roadside café during transfer (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Tasca in Lagoa town — prato do dia with grilled fish or pork, house wine (~€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reloadable Algarve bus card (Vamus) at Faro Airport or Lagoa for cheap local transport throughout the trip. September weather is warm (24–28°C) and seas are still swimmable.

day_by_day.morning: Walk the iconic Praia da Marinha clifftop trail southward toward Praia de Benagil (approx 3 km one way). Enjoy dramatic sea arches, grottos, and turquoise coves — completely free. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Praia da Marinha beach. Rent a kayak or paddleboard locally (~€15/hour) to explore the sea caves and grottos around the headland — a budget-friendly alternative to expensive boat tours. Alternatively, book a budget group kayak tour to Benagil Cave (~€25–30 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Cook a simple meal using a nearby mini-market (pick up local cheese, presunto, bread, olives, and a bottle of Algarve wine for under €10 total).

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hotel or nearby café (~€3)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from mini-market eaten on the beach — local bread, cheese, fruit (~€5)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — charcuterie board with local wine (~€10 total)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Arrive at the beach early morning to secure a spot — it gets busy by midday even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local Vamus bus to Carvoeiro village (~15 min, ~€1.50). Explore the charming whitewashed fishing village and its small beach. Walk the Algar Seco boardwalk — a free coastal rock formation walkway with extraordinary limestone sculptures carved by the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the free Carvoeiro–Vale de Centianes coastal trail (approx 4 km round trip) past hidden cove beaches. Swim at Praia do Carvalho, a secluded beach accessed via a tunnel through the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Carvoeiro for dinner. Visit a local restaurant on the beachfront square — try grilled sardines or cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew). Look for early-bird menus or tourist menus (€12–15 for 3 courses).

meals.breakfast: Pastel de nata and galão coffee at a Carvoeiro café (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at the beach — prego (steak roll) or tosta mista (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant in Carvoeiro — grilled sardines with salad and house wine (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is a short, cheap bus ride from Lagoa. The Algar Seco walkway is free and takes about 30–45 minutes to explore. Wear sturdy shoes on the coastal paths.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Visit Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's famous Algarve winery) near Guia, just north of Lagoa (~20 min by bus or taxi). Book a budget cellar tour and tasting in advance (~€10–15 per person). Learn about Algarve wine production and taste local Negra Mole and Arinto varietals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lagoa town to visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the Algarve's most important wine cooperatives. Tour the facilities and taste local wines affordably (~€5–8 for a tasting flight). Purchase a bottle of local wine to take back.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel. Open your purchased bottle of Lagoa cooperative wine. Prepare a simple pasta or pick up a rotisserie chicken from a local supermarket for a cheap, satisfying dinner.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fruit, and coffee at the hotel or local café (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the winery — soup and sandwich (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — rotisserie chicken from supermarket with salad and local wine (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa wine cooperative is budget-friendly and offers authentic tastings without the tourist markup. Call ahead to confirm opening times. The region's wines are excellent value — full bottles often cost €4–7 at the cooperative.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the Vamus bus from Lagoa (~20 min, ~€1.50). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) — one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Entry fee is around €3–4. Explore the ramparts with sweeping views over the Algarve interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander Silves old town — visit the Gothic Cathedral (free), browse the local market (if it's a Saturday, the market is excellent), and walk along the Arade River. Stop at a local café for a bifana (pork sandwich) lunch. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (~€2 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus. Dinner at a local restaurant in Lagoa town — try bacalhau (salt cod) prepared in a traditional style. Look for 'menu do dia' deals.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast before departure (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Bifana sandwich and local beer in Silves old town (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Traditional bacalhau dish at a Lagoa restaurant with house wine (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit inland Algarve town with 3,000 years of history. The castle alone is worth the trip. If visiting on the third Saturday of the month, there's a medieval market. Silves is also surrounded by orange groves.

day_by_day.morning: Take the bus west to Portimão (~30 min, ~€2). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday mornings, otherwise ~€3) — a fascinating museum built inside a former sardine canning factory with excellent exhibits on local history and fishing culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a charming, less touristy fishing village. Explore the cobbled streets, the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free), and the quieter beaches. Swim at Praia Grande de Ferragudo.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Ferragudo — fresh grilled fish at a local tasca overlooking the river. The seafood here is excellent and more affordable than in Portimão's tourist centre.

meals.breakfast: Pastel de nata and espresso in Portimão (~€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near the beach in Ferragudo — prego or soup (~€5–6)
meals.dinner: Grilled fish at a Ferragudo riverside tasca — dorada or robalo with salad (~€12–14)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a hidden gem often overlooked by tourists who stay in Portimão. The village has a very authentic feel. The bus between Portimão and Lagoa runs frequently. Portimão is also famous for its sardine grilling in August, but September still has great seafood.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and beach morning at Praia da Marinha. Swim, snorkel (bring your own mask or rent cheaply locally), and relax. The water in September is at its warmest (~22–23°C). Explore the rock pools at low tide — check tide times the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Albandeira — a secluded, quieter cove beach a short walk east of Praia da Marinha. Bring a picnic. Alternatively, hike the full Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Sete Vales Suspensos) starting from Praia da Marinha — a stunning 5.7 km free coastal trail to Praia de Vale Covo.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Marinha — enjoy a glass of local wine or a Super Bock beer while watching the sun set over the Atlantic. Cook or self-cater dinner at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel or nearby café (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from mini-market — local olives, cheese, tomatoes, bread (~€6)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with tinned tuna and local olive oil, salad, wine (~€7)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a rest and recharge day. The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of the most beautiful coastal walks in Europe and is completely free. Download an offline map (Maps.me or AllTrails) before heading out. Wear sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Lagos — take the bus (~45 min from Portimão, ~€3). Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a dramatic series of golden limestone sea stacks and arches just south of Lagos town. The viewpoint is free. Hike down the steps to the waterline for close-up views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town — walk the medieval city walls (free), visit Igreja de Santo António (~€4 entry with the municipal museum), and browse the vibrant market square. Walk along Meia Praia beach (a long, flat, family-friendly beach north of Lagos).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos — try a restaurant on Rua 25 de Abril for good-value local food. Lagos has a lively budget dining scene with plenty of €10–14 mains. Try local cataplana or frango piri-piri.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry in Lagos town on arrival (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Ponta da Piedade — sandwich and juice (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Lagos old town — cataplana or grilled chicken with wine (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the Algarve's most popular towns but still very manageable in September after the August peak. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning light. The boat tours from Lagos harbour to the sea caves are around €15–20 if you want to add that.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (between Lagoa and Portimão). Book a budget vineyard tour and tasting (~€10–15). The estate grows Syrah, Touriga Nacional, and Viognier. Beautiful vineyard setting with sculpture garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, head to Praia de Armação de Pêra — a long, wide Atlantic beach about 15 km east of Lagoa (reachable by bus). Swim and relax on one of the Algarve's longest beaches. The town is less glamorous but very affordable.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Armação de Pêra — a local seafood restaurant near the beach. The town caters to domestic Portuguese tourists so prices are lower than in more international resort towns.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt and coffee at the hotel before the winery visit (~€3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a nearby café — soup and bread (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant in Armação de Pêra — mixed fish grill with local wine (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the most scenic wineries in the Algarve. Book tours in advance via their website. September is harvest season so you may see grape picking in action — a special bonus experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus east to Albufeira (~30 min from Lagoa, ~€2). Explore the old town — the original fishing village area around Rua Cândido dos Reis and Praça Miguel Bombarda is charming and far removed from the party-resort image. Visit the free clifftop viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira old town — a small cove beach with colourful fishing boats. Take a short taxi or bus to Praia de São Rafael or Praia da Galé — quieter, more scenic beaches west of Albufeira.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for dinner. Visit the weekly local market in Lagoa if it coincides (check schedule locally). Cook at accommodation or grab a cheap churrasqueira (rotisserie grill) takeaway — half a chicken with chips costs around €5–7.

meals.breakfast: Pastel de nata and galão at a Albufeira café (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines at a beachside snack bar in Albufeira old town (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Churrasqueira takeaway back at Lagoa — half chicken, chips, and salad (~€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Stick to Albufeira's old town and avoid the Strip (Avenida Sá Carneiro) which is noisy and expensive. The old town has genuine Portuguese character. September sees far fewer rowdy tourists than July–August.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Spend the morning swimming, snorkelling, and exploring the coastal rock formations. This is your last full beach day so savour it. Bring a picnic breakfast to eat on the cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal path in the opposite direction (east) toward Praia de Vale de Centeanes. Explore the quieter coves along the way. Alternatively, rent a bicycle in Lagoa town (~€10–15/day) and cycle the flat inland roads through the countryside and traditional villages.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the penultimate evening — visit a well-reviewed local restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro. Try a regional cataplana (seafood or pork and clams) — a true Algarve speciality. Budget €18–22 per person with wine.

meals.breakfast: Picnic breakfast on the clifftops — yogurt, fruit, pastry from mini-market (~€4)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — grilled fish sandwich and local beer (~€7–9)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at a Carvoeiro or Lagoa restaurant — cataplana de marisco with wine (~€20–22)

day_by_day.notes: Cataplana is the quintessential Algarve dish and worth the slightly higher spend. It's typically cooked for two people in a copper clam-shaped pot. Ask restaurants if they have a half-portion option to save cost.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Take the bus from Portimão (~1.5 hours, ~€4–5). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a massive 15th-century fortress used by Henry the Navigator to plan Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a taxi to Cabo de São Vicente (5 km from Sagres) — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. The lighthouse and clifftop views over the crashing Atlantic are breathtaking and completely free to visit. Watch surfers at Praia do Tonel below the fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus (allow 2 hours travel time). Last evening — pack bags and enjoy a farewell dinner at your favourite local spot discovered during the trip. Raise a glass of Lagoa cooperative wine to a wonderful Algarve adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early coffee and toast before departure (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Café in Sagres village — soup, sandwich, and coffee (~€7–9)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at favourite local restaurant in Lagoa — whatever you enjoyed most this trip (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is very windy even in September — bring a light layer. The bus journey is long but scenic. Alternatively, consider renting a car just for this day (~€25–35) to see more of the Costa Vicentina Natural Park. Cabo de São Vicente sunsets are legendary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Praia da Marinha clifftops. Take photos, breathe the sea air, and soak in the views. Pack remaining bags and check out of the accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on return flight time: if afternoon/evening flight, take the bus or pre-booked transfer to Faro Airport (~1–1.5 hours from Lagoa). Arrive at the airport with 2 hours to spare. Browse duty-free for a bottle of Algarve wine or ginjinha liqueur as a souvenir (~€5–10). If morning flight, depart directly after breakfast.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, cliffs, and authentic Portuguese culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and espresso at a local café — a perfect send-off (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport café or grab a prego sandwich to go (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days: Accommodation (variable), Local transport ~€30–40 total, Food ~€15–20/day average, Activities and wine tastings ~€80–100 total, Souvenirs ~€20–30. Total non-accommodation spend approximately €350–450 for 13 days. Pre-book the Faro airport transfer in advance for best rates (~€20–25 shared shuttle).

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up pre-booked rental car (essential for Algarve exploration), and drive ~45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a gentle first look at Praia da Marinha — walk the clifftop trail above the beach to take in the iconic golden limestone rock formations and turquoise water. No need to descend the steep steps today; just enjoy the panoramic views and decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (~10 min drive), a charming fishing village with a small beach, whitewashed houses, and a relaxed atmosphere. Browse the seafront promenade and find a terrace restaurant for your first Algarve dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a pastry and coffee at Faro Airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at a café near the airport or en route — try a 'tosta mista' and galão (milky coffee) at a roadside café
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant in Carvoeiro — mid-range seafood restaurant with ocean views; try the grilled sea bass (robalo) or cataplana de marisco (seafood stew). Budget ~€25–35 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Rental car is strongly recommended for this itinerary. Book in advance for September. Praia da Marinha's beach access involves steep wooden steps — save the descent for Day 2 when rested. September is warm (24–28°C), sunny, and less crowded than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day properly at Praia da Marinha — descend the wooden steps to one of the Algarve's most photographed beaches. Swim in the crystal-clear water, explore the sea caves and rock arches accessible by wading at low tide (check tide times the night before). Arrive early (~9:30am) for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Algar Seco, a dramatic rock formation and natural sea pool near Carvoeiro. Walk the boardwalk trail along the cliffs and enjoy the sculpted limestone formations. Afterwards, head to Praia de Benagil and book a kayak or SUP tour to visit the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Tours depart from the beach (~€15–20 per person, 1.5 hrs).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Drive to Lagoa town (~15 min) for dinner in a local tasca — a more authentic, budget-friendly experience away from the tourist coast.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a nearby café — fresh fruit, yogurt, toast with local honey, and espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia da Marinha or grab a grilled fish sandwich and cold beer at the small beach kiosk near Benagil
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa or similar local tasca — try bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) or pork secretos with migas. Budget ~€15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave tours sell out fast in September — book online the evening before. Low tide is best for rock pool exploration at Praia da Marinha. Wear water shoes for the rocky beach.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~25 minutes west to Silves, the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River. Explore the Gothic Cathedral of Silves next door.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting afternoon! The Algarve has a growing wine scene. Visit Quinta dos Vales (~15 min from Silves), a well-regarded estate near Estômbar offering guided vineyard tours and tastings of their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés. Book in advance. (~€15–25 per person for a tasting session). Alternatively visit Quinta da Penina or Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery near Guia).
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Silves for a relaxed evening — the town has excellent mid-range restaurants with riverside terraces.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a café in Carvoeiro before departure
meals.lunch: Café/restaurant near Silves castle — try a bifanas (pork sandwich) or a simple prato do dia (dish of the day) for €8–12
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a local institution famous for cataplana and fresh shellfish. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for tours. Silves is best explored on foot — park near the river. The castle is worth at least 90 minutes. September is harvest season in many Algarve vineyards — you may catch grape-picking activity.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~50 minutes west to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) — the dramatic southwestern tip of continental Europe. Walk the clifftops, visit the lighthouse, and feel the raw Atlantic wind. The views are extraordinary. Then explore the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a historic fortress with a mysterious wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) etched into the ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back east along the western Algarve coast, stopping at Praia do Amado — a world-class surf beach with a wilder, more rugged feel than the south-coast beaches. Watch surfers or take a beginner surf lesson (~€35–45 with board and wetsuit). Continue to the beautiful Praia de Odeceixe if time allows (near the Alentejo border).
day_by_day.evening: Stop in Lagos (~30 min east of Sagres) for dinner — a vibrant town with excellent restaurants, bars, and a lively but not overwhelming nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the drive
meals.lunch: Café Sagres or a snack bar near the cape — simple grilled fish, soup, and bread. Very affordable (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: : A Forja Restaurant in Lagos or Casinha do Petisco — try the grilled tuna steak (atum) or arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice). Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent is windier and cooler than the south coast — bring a light layer. The drive from Praia da Marinha to Sagres takes about 50–55 minutes. This is a long day (full day road trip) — start by 8:30am. Lagos is about 30 min from the hotel on the return.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos more thoroughly. Walk the old town walls, visit the Ponta da Piedade — a stunning series of golden rock towers, grottos, and arches just south of Lagos. Walk the clifftop path (free) or take a boat tour from Lagos marina to see the caves from the water (~€15–20, 45 min). Visit the small but moving Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum, €3).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at one of Lagos's beautiful beaches — Meia Praia (long sandy beach, good for swimming) or Praia Dona Ana (sheltered cove, stunning scenery). Rent a sunbed and umbrella (~€10–15 for two) and enjoy a classic beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos's lively Saturday evening scene. The town has a great mix of traditional tascas and modern restaurants. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine at a rooftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Lusitana or similar café in Lagos old town — pastel de nata, orange juice, and espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic supplies from the Lagos municipal market (Mercado Municipal) — local cheese, presunto, olives, fresh bread, and fruit. Eat on the clifftops at Ponta da Piedade.
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant overlooking Praia de Camilo — romantic clifftop setting, excellent seafood. Budget ~€30–40 per person. Book ahead for Saturday.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Lagos can be busy in September — arrive at Ponta da Piedade before 10am for fewer crowds. The boat tour from Lagos marina is a great option if you haven't done Benagil Cave yet. Drive back to Praia da Marinha is about 30 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Spend a slow morning at Praia da Marinha — swim, snorkel (the water is crystal clear and the marine life is excellent), or simply read on the beach. The beach is quieter on Sunday mornings once the weekend day-trippers leave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 10 minutes to Praia de Albandeira or Praia de Armação de Pêra — a longer, wider beach better suited for a long swim and a walk. Armação de Pêra has a small old fishing village section worth exploring. Alternatively, rent a kayak or paddleboard from Marinha Beach (~€15/hr) and explore the sea caves independently.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the clifftops near the hotel — bring a bottle of local rosé and watch the sun dip toward the Atlantic. Dinner in Porches or Lagoa — quieter and more local than the beach towns.

meals.breakfast: Lazy hotel breakfast or a nearby café — scrambled eggs, toast, fresh orange juice (Algarve oranges are exceptional)
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk or snack bar at Armação de Pêra — prego no pão (steak sandwich), chips, and cold Sagres beer
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (~15 min drive) — beautiful riverside village, excellent grilled fish and seafood. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate slow day — the itinerary is balanced between activity and rest. Snorkel gear can be rented in Carvoeiro or bought cheaply at local sports shops. Ferragudo is a hidden gem worth visiting in the evening when day visitors have left.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~1 hour east to Faro, the Algarve's capital. Visit the Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the Arco da Vila, explore the peaceful Cathedral (Sé de Faro, €3.50, climb the tower for views), and visit the unusual Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones) inside the Carmo Church (~€4).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro's pier to the Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro — pristine barrier islands within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. These long, flat sandy islands backed by the lagoon are stunning and feel completely different from the rocky west Algarve coast. Ferry runs regularly (~€3–5 return). Swim, walk, and enjoy the wild, undeveloped landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro before driving back. Faro has an excellent restaurant scene that is underrated by tourists who rush through.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel before departing, or stop at a pastelaria in Faro old town upon arrival
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha Deserta or the small restaurant/bar on the island (limited menu, bring snacks as backup)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town — excellent regional Algarve cuisine in a historic building. Try the cataplana or the amêijoas na cataplana (clams). Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check Ria Formosa ferry schedules in advance — last ferry back from the islands is usually late afternoon/early evening. Faro old town is compact and walkable. Allow 2–3 hours for the city exploration. Drive back to Praia da Marinha is about 55 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~45 minutes east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, castle ruins (free entry to gardens), the Igreja da Misericórdia, and the charming grid of cobblestone streets lined with terracotta-roofed townhouses. Climb to the castle for views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry or water taxi from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a magnificent barrier island with one of the finest beaches in Portugal. The beach stretches for kilometers in both directions, backed by dunes and the Ria Formosa lagoon. Swim, walk, and enjoy the wild Atlantic-meets-lagoon landscape. Ferry runs frequently (~€2 return).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before returning — the town has excellent seafood restaurants along the Gilão River.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or café in Carvoeiro before departing
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Ilha de Tavira beach — fresh grilled fish, salad, and cold beer with feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — riverside terrace, excellent grilled fish and regional specials. Budget ~€20–28 per person. Or try Quatro Águas near the ferry dock for a more upscale experience (~€30–40).

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is the most 'un-touristy' major Algarve town — it has a genuine Portuguese feel. September is ideal — warm but not overcrowded. The island beach is very long; walk 15–20 minutes from the ferry dock to find more secluded spots. Drive back is about 55 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Wine and cork country excursion. Drive north ~40 minutes into the Algarve interior (Serra do Caldeirão foothills) toward Monchique or the cork oak forests near Silves. Visit a local quinta for a morning wine tasting — try Quinta do Francês near Silves or Quinta da Tôr near Loulé, both offering tastings of Algarve DOC wines. The Algarve's reds (especially Negra Mole and Castelão blends) and medronho (arbutus berry brandy) are worth discovering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to Monchique — a beautiful mountain village at 458m altitude with a completely different microclimate and landscape (lush, green, forested). Explore the village, visit the ruined Franciscan convent, and taste the local firewater medronho at a village bar. Drive up to Fóia peak (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for sweeping views over the entire coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast via a scenic mountain road. Dinner in Portimão or Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — hearty mountain food including espetada (meat skewers), presunto, and local cheeses. Very affordable (~€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca da Adriana in Carvoeiro or a Portimão riverside restaurant — grilled dourada (sea bream) or fresh tuna. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast — bring a light layer. The medronho brandy is potent (40–50% ABV) — taste in small quantities during the winery visit. The mountain road from Monchique to the coast via Caldas de Monchique is beautiful and worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Meia Praia — a 4km long sandy beach near Lagos, one of the longest in the Algarve. Ideal for a long morning swim, beach walk, and total relaxation. The beach is wide and the water is calmer than the rockier cove beaches. Rent sunbeds and an umbrella for the day (~€12–15 for two).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Portimão for a cultural and culinary afternoon. The Museu de Portimão (free or €3) is an excellent museum built inside a converted fish cannery — fascinating exhibits on the sardine canning industry that defined the Algarve economy. Walk along the Arade River waterfront and browse the market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its sardine grilling culture — the riverside area near the old bridge has numerous restaurants specializing in charcoal-grilled sardines. This is an unmissable Algarve experience, especially in September when sardines are at their fattest and most flavorful.

meals.breakfast: Café near Meia Praia or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant at Meia Praia — fresh salads, grilled fish, and cold white wine
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré or Churrasqueira Valdemar on the Portimão riverside — charcoal-grilled sardines with boiled potatoes, peppers, and salad. Budget ~€15–20 per person. Simple, authentic, and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: September is the absolute best month for sardines in Portugal — they are larger and richer than the summer months. The Museu de Portimão is surprisingly good and air-conditioned — perfect for a warm afternoon. Portimão is 20 minutes from Praia da Marinha.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~35 minutes east to Loulé — the Algarve's largest inland town and a center of traditional crafts. Visit the covered Mercado de Loulé (one of the best markets in the Algarve — especially good on Saturday morning, but open daily). Browse stalls selling local honey, almonds, figs, carob, cheeses, and charcuterie. Walk through the Moorish-influenced old town and visit the castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Vilamoura (~20 min from Loulé) — the Algarve's most famous marina resort. Walk the glittering marina, visit the Roman ruins of Cerro da Vila (€2, surprisingly impressive), and if interested, arrange an afternoon dolphin watching boat trip from the marina (~€35–45, 2.5 hrs) — September is excellent for dolphin sightings in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Vilamoura marina atmosphere for sunset drinks, then head back toward Lagoa for a quieter dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café at Loulé market — fresh pastries, local honey, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at a tasca in Loulé old town — prato do dia with soup, main, and drink for €10–13
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dois Irmãos in Portimão (historic institution since 1927) or a local restaurant in Lagoa — fresh grilled fish or arroz de tamboril (monkfish rice). Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Loulé Saturday market is the best in the Algarve — if you can shift Day 11 activities to Saturday, it's worth it. The dolphin watching trips from Vilamoura are well-regarded — common and bottlenose dolphins are regularly spotted. Book in advance for September weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to Praia da Marinha one last time. Swim, snorkel, and explore the sea caves you may have missed earlier in the trip. Take photos of the extraordinary rock formations in the morning light. Soak in the beauty of what many consider the most beautiful beach in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) — a famous ceramics studio and shop near the hotel (~10 min drive) where you can watch artisans hand-painting traditional Algarve azulejo-style tiles and pottery. Buy a piece as a meaningful souvenir. Then drive to Ferragudo — the picturesque fishing village across the Arade River from Portimão — for a final afternoon stroll through its whitewashed streets and clifftop castle views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly for your last night. Choose a special restaurant for a memorable final meal celebrating 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Ferragudo — fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and a glass of chilled Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Vila Joya (if budget allows — Michelin-starred, €150+ pp) or a more balanced splurge at Sueste in Ferragudo or Henrique Leis near Almancil (~€50–70 pp). Alternatively, a beautiful final dinner at a clifftop restaurant in Carvoeiro with a bottle of good Algarve wine. Toast to a wonderful trip.

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is a wonderful stop — pieces are hand-made and reasonably priced (€15–80 for most items). Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and photogenic villages in the Algarve — far less touristy than Carvoeiro or Lagos. Pack your bags tonight for an easy morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Take one last walk along the clifftops above Praia da Marinha. Pack any remaining souvenirs — local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos or Morgados), medronho, or a bottle of Algarve wine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (~45 minutes from Praia da Marinha). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for car return, check-in, and security. The Algarve airport is small but can have queues on Sunday afternoons in September.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 wonderful days in one of Europe's most beautiful coastal regions.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a café near the hotel — a proper Portuguese farewell
meals.lunch: Airport café or a final stop at a roadside café en route to Faro — a simple bifana or tosta mista
meals.dinner: On the flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank — there are petrol stations on the EN125 road near Faro Airport. Buy last-minute Algarve products at the airport (they have a reasonable selection of local wines, honey, and sweets). Check flight time carefully and work backwards for departure from the hotel — allow 45 min drive + 2 hours at airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min scenic drive along the EN125). Enjoy a welcome bottle of chilled Vinho Verde upon check-in and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely first stroll down to Praia da Marinha — one of the most photographed beaches in the Algarve. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, hidden sea caves, and turquoise coves. Swim or simply absorb the scenery. The beach is a 5-minute walk from the boutique stay.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the clifftop terrace of your boutique stay or at a nearby viewpoint overlooking the Atlantic. Then head to dinner at a curated local restaurant in Carvoeiro village (10-min drive), known for its intimate seafood dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day. Welcome snack platter and sparkling wine provided at the boutique stay upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the boutique stay's private terrace or a nearby café — fresh local bread, charcuterie, olives, and regional cheeses.
meals.dinner: Dinner at O Castelo (Carvoeiro) — a premium clifftop restaurant serving grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), and regional wines. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if flight allows. Pack beach essentials in carry-on for immediate afternoon use. September in the Algarve is warm (~26°C), sunny, and ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking and sea cave tour departing from Praia da Marinha. Paddle through the iconic arches, grottos, and hidden coves of the Benagil coastline — one of the most spectacular stretches of coastline in Europe. A professional guide leads a small-group premium experience (~2.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the legendary Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — accessible by kayak or private boat. Spend time inside the cathedral-like cavern, photograph the natural skylight, and explore the adjacent beaches only accessible by water. Return to the boutique stay for a poolside rest and light refreshment.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise along the Marinha-Benagil coastline. Sip chilled Alentejo white wine and local sparkling water as you watch the cliffs turn gold and amber at dusk. Return to shore for a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — freshly squeezed orange juice, local pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, artisan cheeses, and Portuguese coffee (bica).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Restaurante Benagil — grilled octopus salad, fresh sardines, and a glass of chilled Alvarinho.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro) — Michelin-starred fine dining featuring tasting menus inspired by Algarve's land and sea. Pair with sommelier-selected Portuguese wines.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour and sunset boat cruise at least 48 hours in advance. Bon Bon is Michelin-starred — reservation essential weeks ahead. Wear reef-safe sunscreen for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting experience at Quinta dos Vales (Estômbar, ~20-min drive) — one of the Algarve's most prestigious wine estates. Enjoy a guided vineyard walk, learn about the unique terroir of southern Portugal, and taste award-winning reds, whites, and rosés, including their signature Algarve DO wines. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculpture art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine journey with a visit to Adega do Cantor (Guia, ~25 min) — a celebrated winery co-founded by Sir Cliff Richard, known for its Vida Nova and Onda Nova labels. Enjoy a VIP cellar tour and seated tasting with paired local charcuterie and cheese boards.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private in-room wine and cheese pairing prepared by the hotel using bottles selected during the day's tastings. Early evening walk along the clifftop path at Praia da Marinha as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — acai bowls, local honey, almond pastries, fresh fruit platters, and specialty Portuguese coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch provided by Quinta dos Vales on the vineyard terrace — regional charcuterie, artisan bread, olives, figs, and paired estate wines.
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining experience — boutique stay chef prepares a 3-course seasonal Algarvian menu featuring local catch, roasted vegetables, and almond-based desserts (amendoins). Paired with wines from the day's tastings.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private driver for the full wine tour day — do not self-drive after tastings. Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for VIP experiences. Bring a small cooler bag to transport wine purchases back to the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~25-min drive). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish fortresses in Portugal. Walk the ancient walls, explore the archaeological museum within, and enjoy sweeping views over the orange and cork oak countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Silves' charming old town — visit the Gothic Cathedral of Silves (Sé de Silves), browse local artisan shops, and stop at the municipal market for fresh figs, almonds, and carob products unique to the region. Drive back via the EN124 scenic route through citrus groves and cork forests.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha area. Enjoy a pre-dinner Negroni or Aperol Spritz at the boutique stay's bar. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Lagos (~35 min) — a vibrant coastal town with an excellent fine dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — warm croissants, local jams, scrambled eggs with truffle, smoked ham, fresh orange juice, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Marisqueira Rui — a beloved local institution serving exceptional percebes (barnacles), tiger prawns, and cataplana, paired with crisp Alentejo white wine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vistas Restaurant at Monte Santo Resort (Lagos) — elevated Algarvian cuisine with panoramic views, featuring aged Alentejo beef, local seafood, and an extensive Portuguese wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Silves Castle entrance fee is minimal — worth arriving early to avoid afternoon heat. Silves is particularly atmospheric on Friday evenings if there is a local market. Confirm Lagos restaurant reservation 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter departing from Portimão Marina (~20-min drive). Sail west along the dramatic coastline toward Ponta da Piedade and Lagos Bay. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters above vibrant marine life, explore sea arches by dinghy, and relax on the yacht's deck with chilled champagne and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at a secluded cove accessible only by boat for a private swim and sunbathing session. The yacht crew serves a gourmet onboard lunch. Sail back to Portimão Marina in the late afternoon. Optional stop at the Portimão waterfront promenade for a short walk.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Praia da Rocha (adjacent to Portimão) at sunset — a wide golden beach framed by ochre cliffs, beautiful at golden hour. Then dinner at a premium riverside restaurant in Portimão.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — Greek yogurt with local honey and almonds, avocado toast with poached eggs, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard yacht lunch prepared by crew — chilled seafood platter (oysters, prawns, smoked salmon), artisan cheeses, crusty bread, and chilled Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Titanic (Portimão) — a long-standing fine dining institution renowned for its fresh Atlantic seafood, grilled fish, and extensive wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Private yacht charter (6–8 hours) should be booked at least one week in advance through a reputable Portimão charter company. Bring SPF 50+, a hat, and a light cover-up for the boat. September seas are calm and ideal for sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy an extended boutique breakfast on the terrace, and take a slow morning walk along the clifftop trail between Praia da Marinha and Praia de Albandeira. This 3km coastal path offers some of the most breathtaking cliff formations and hidden beach viewpoints in the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a luxury spa afternoon at the boutique stay or at a nearby premium spa (e.g., Vila Vita Parc Resort & Spa, Porches — 15-min drive). Choose from a couples' massage, Algarvian honey and almond body wrap, or a hydrotherapy circuit. Followed by pool relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the boutique stay terrace. Elegant dinner at Vila Vita Parc's Ocean Restaurant — a double Michelin-starred experience considered one of the finest in Portugal, with a legendary wine cellar of 50,000+ bottles.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet boutique breakfast — eggs any style, smoked fish selection, fresh pastries, tropical fruit, granola, and specialty teas and coffees.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — gazpacho, grilled vegetable bruschetta, and fresh fruit sorbet.
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Ocean Restaurant, Vila Vita Parc (Michelin 2-star) — a multi-course culinary journey featuring hyper-local Algarvian ingredients with Japanese-influenced techniques by Chef Hans Neuner. Wine pairing included.

day_by_day.notes: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc is one of the most sought-after reservations in Portugal — book weeks or months in advance. Dress code is smart elegant. The spa at Vila Vita Parc is world-class and treatments should also be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the western Algarve — drive or private transfer to Sagres (~1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress), perched on a windswept promontory at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the historic compass rose, the chapel, and the stunning views over the Atlantic where two oceans meet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent) — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the world on dramatic 70-meter cliffs. Explore the lighthouse and artisan market stalls selling local crafts. Drive back east via the EN268 through the Costa Vicentina natural park.
day_by_day.evening: Stop in Lagos on the return journey for a sunset drink at a rooftop bar. Dinner in Lagos before returning to Praia da Marinha.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — packed to-go option if departing early, or full sit-down breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Sagres Restaurant (Sagres village) — fresh grilled fish of the day, local clams, and regional wine in a relaxed Atlantic-view setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Casinha do Petisco (Lagos) — a beloved premium local restaurant with outstanding cataplana dishes, fresh percebes, and a curated Portuguese wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is noticeably windier and cooler than the central Algarve — bring a light jacket. The drive to Sagres is scenic and worth taking the coastal N268 route. Cabo de São Vicente at sunset is extraordinary if timing allows on the return.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep safari through the Serra de Monchique mountain range (~40-min drive inland). Explore the lush green hills, eucalyptus and pine forests, and traditional villages of the Algarve's interior. Visit the thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique and the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve with panoramic views to the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monchique town — browse local artisan shops for medronho (arbutus berry brandy), smoked sausages, and handmade wooden crafts. Visit a local distillery for a private medronho tasting experience. Return to the boutique stay via scenic mountain roads.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay. Private sunset yoga or meditation session on the clifftop arranged through the hotel. Followed by a quiet, intimate dinner.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — warm pastéis de nata, fresh fruit, yogurt, eggs, and Portuguese coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Luar da Fóia (Monchique summit) — traditional Algarvian mountain cuisine featuring roasted kid goat (cabrito), black pork (porco preto), and regional wines with stunning panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo, ~15-min drive) — a premium riverside seafood restaurant with exceptional fresh fish, lobster, and an outstanding wine list overlooking the Arade River estuary.

day_by_day.notes: The jeep safari should be arranged through a reputable premium operator — small group or private tours recommended. Medronho is very strong (45%+ ABV) — taste responsibly. Ferragudo is a beautifully preserved fishing village worth exploring briefly before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine and olive oil estate tour at Herdade dos Grous or a nearby premium Alentejo estate accessible as a day trip (~1.5-hour drive north into Alentejo). Explore the vast cork oak and olive groves, tour the modern winery, and participate in an in-depth vertical wine tasting of their flagship reds and whites with the estate's sommelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch among the vines followed by an olive oil tasting — learn to distinguish between varietals, acidity levels, and harvest timings. Purchase premium bottles to take home. Scenic drive back through the rolling Alentejo plains and cork forests toward the Algarve coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha. Unwind with a glass of the day's wine on the terrace. Casual but premium dinner close to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — full spread with local produce, eggs, pastries, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Estate picnic lunch — regional charcuterie (presunto, chouriço), artisan cheeses, sourdough bread, olives, and paired estate wines served among the vineyards.
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Ver Tavira (Carvoeiro) — a premium cliffside restaurant with fresh Atlantic fish, exceptional tuna tataki, and a thoughtful wine list.

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo day trip is a longer drive — arrange a private driver. This is the heart of Portugal's finest wine country and pairs perfectly with the Algarve trip. Book the estate experience in advance for a VIP private tour.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at Praia da Marinha — rent premium sun loungers and a private beach umbrella setup. Swim in the crystal-clear September waters (still warm at ~22°C sea temperature). Explore the rock pools and natural arches at the base of the cliffs accessible at low tide. Bring snorkeling gear for an underwater exploration of the marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Armação de Pêra beach (~20-min drive west) — a wide, sweeping sandy beach perfect for a long afternoon walk. Explore the small whitewashed Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched dramatically on a clifftop promontory. Browse the local fish market stalls along the promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for sunset cocktails. Premium dinner at a restaurant in Albufeira's old town (~30-min drive east) — one of the Algarve's most vibrant evening destinations.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — smoothie bowls, eggs Florentine, local pastries, and cold-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium beach club near Praia da Marinha — grilled sea bream, avocado salad, and a chilled glass of Alvarinho.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Gordo (Albufeira old town) — a renowned premium restaurant specializing in traditional Portuguese petiscos elevated to fine dining level, with an exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times for Praia da Marinha rock pool access — low tide reveals the most spectacular formations. Albufeira old town is best explored on foot — park at the clifftop car park and walk down to the historic center.

day_by_day.morning: Private stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) lesson or guided coastal SUP tour departing from Praia da Marinha or Praia de Albandeira. Glide along the calm morning waters past sea arches and golden cliffs with a certified instructor. September mornings offer glassy, calm sea conditions ideal for paddleboarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Loulé (~40-min drive) — the cultural and artisan capital of the Algarve. Explore the stunning Moorish-influenced covered market (Mercado de Loulé), browse handcrafted copper goods, leather items, and local produce. Visit the Loulé Castle ruins and the historic old quarter. Stop at a local pastelaria for a freshly baked pastel de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Arrange a private in-villa chef experience — a local premium chef comes to the boutique stay and prepares a bespoke 5-course Algarvian tasting menu in your suite or on the terrace, paired with hand-selected Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — full gourmet spread with local seasonal fruits, artisan pastries, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Loulé at Bica Velha — one of the oldest and most celebrated restaurants in the Algarve, known for its traditional cataplana, grilled meats, and exceptional wine list.
meals.dinner: Private in-villa chef experience — 5-course tasting menu featuring local lobster bisque, Algarvian sea bass ceviche, cataplana de bivalves, slow-roasted Alentejo lamb, and carob and almond tart. Paired with a curated selection of Portuguese wines.

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is most vibrant on Saturday mornings — if adjusting the itinerary, consider moving this visit to Day 12 Saturday morning for the full market experience. Book the private chef experience through the boutique stay concierge at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Loulé Saturday Market (if rescheduled from Day 11) OR spend the morning at Praia de Albandeira — a smaller, more secluded beach adjacent to Praia da Marinha, accessible via a short clifftop walk. Relax on the golden sand, swim, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the weekend crowds arrive. Alternatively, arrange a private morning golf session at one of the nearby premium courses (Vale do Lobo or Quinta do Lago, ~45 min east).
day_by_day.afternoon: Quinta do Lago / Vale do Lobo area exploration (~45-min drive east) — home to some of Europe's finest golf courses and luxury estates. Walk the famous Quinta do Lago nature trail around the Ria Formosa lagoon, spot flamingos and migratory birds, and enjoy the upscale resort atmosphere. Visit the Quinta Shopping boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell premium dinner at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants — a fitting conclusion to the culinary journey of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — a special extended Saturday breakfast with fresh pastries, smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, fruit platters, and celebratory mimosas.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Casa do Lago (Quinta do Lago) — an iconic lakeside restaurant with stunning Ria Formosa views, serving premium seafood and Mediterranean dishes with exceptional wine service.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Gusto by Heinz Beck (Conrad Algarve, Quinta do Lago) — a Michelin-starred experience by legendary chef Heinz Beck, featuring Italian-Portuguese fusion cuisine of the highest caliber. Full wine pairing recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Gusto by Heinz Beck reservation is essential — book well in advance. Vale do Lobo and Quinta do Lago golf courses require advance tee time booking. The Ria Formosa nature walk is free and spectacular — bring binoculars for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — a slow, indulgent breakfast on the boutique stay terrace. Take one last walk down to Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the cliffs and turquoise waters. Collect any last wine or artisan purchases. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the boutique stay. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for the return flight. En route, optional brief stop in the charming village of Alte (~45 min from Faro) — considered one of the most beautiful villages in the Algarve, with a natural spring, whitewashed houses, and a peaceful village square for a final coffee and pastel de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry home premium Portuguese wines, olive oils, medronho, local almonds, and artisan crafts as souvenirs of an extraordinary 13-day Algarve luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended final gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — the full works, savored slowly. Fresh juice, pastries, eggs, smoked fish, local cheeses, and the best bica of the trip.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch in Alte or at the airport — a bifana (pork sandwich) or pastel de nata and espresso at a local café as a final authentic Portuguese moment.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or onboard flight meal — the memories of 13 days of exceptional Algarvian cuisine will more than compensate.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security at Faro Airport. Request a late check-out from the boutique stay if the flight is in the late afternoon or evening — most luxury properties accommodate this for premium guests. Confirm private transfer timing with the driver the evening before.
